writeup: TIC 412057714 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 4.4876 days. The primary eclipse causes the star to dim by 1.21 percent, while a secondary eclipse was detected at 6.0 sigma significance. Automated analysis of TESS photometry yielded a strong Box Least Squares signal-to-noise ratio of 189.2, and pixel-level difference imaging confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 20.1. The centroid offset measured 16.8 arcseconds from the target position. The candidate did not appear in searches across six variable-star catalogs, and the machine-learning screening assigned it a score of 0.96, indicating high confidence that this represents a genuine target rather than instrumental noise or a false positive.
